exposure: Model of care (caseload midwifery, standard hospital care, private obstetric care)
cohort: 1379 low-risk first-time mothers ('standard primipara') at a tertiary teaching hospital in Australia between July 1, 2009 and December 31, 2010
finding: Caseload midwifery was associated with higher rates of spontaneous onset of labor, unassisted vaginal birth, and lower rates of elective cesarean section, as well as lower costs of care compared to standard hospital care and private obstetric care.
mod_finding: Women receiving caseload midwifery had a higher likelihood of unassisted vaginal birth compared to standard hospital care and private obstetric care.
